messages:
Alex: Proposal: introduce a 'soft lift' for partner/internal API keys — temporary, auditable burst above per-key limits that degrades gracefully instead of hard-blocking. Sketch below, want feedback on enforcement + console UX.
Maria: Nice. Is this meant for scheduled ETL jobs or just emergency manual lifts?
Alex: Both. Two modes: 1) emergency one-off (manual, short TTL) 2) scheduled window (time-bound, owner + justification). Both create telemetry events and audit entries.
Sam: Implementation thoughts: token-bucket still primary. Soft lift toggles an additional burst bucket with configurable size + decay. If soft-burst exhausted, fallback to normal rate-limit or slow-path routing.
Sam: Key details: soft-lift should emit metrics: `key.soft_lift.granted`, `key.soft_lift.used_tokens`, `key.soft_lift.expired`, `key.soft_lift.revert_auto` so we can chart usage and cost.
Jordan: Observability: add a per-key sampling stream to trace requests during lifts (1% by default -> 100% for first 5m of a lift). Alert rule: any single key > 10k soft tokens used within 1h -> pager.
Nina: Security: who can grant? Need RBAC: ops team + SREs allowed for internal partner keys. All lifts must require a justification text and link to the ticket/owner. Also retention of the justification in audit log for 1 year.
Maria: Console UX idea: in the key detail page, a small "Request soft lift" button with a modal: fields = reason, TTL (max 24h), approver, cost-estimate toggle. If approver not needed (auto-allowed for tier-1 partners) it still writes an audit entry.
Alex: Agreed. Auto-approve rules: allow list by org id + daily quota. Anything outside that needs approver. Add a checkbox: "auto-revert at TTL" (default true).
Sam: Enforcement nuance: we should apply soft-lift only at routing layer, not change model assignment. So requests still go through the same model and pool but get allowed extra tokens; we can surface a header `x-redwood-softlift=1` for downstream billing/observability.
Sam: Pseudo-config:
```
key_overrides:
  partner-123:
    soft_lift:
      max_tokens: 50000
      ttl_seconds: 3600
      auto_revert: true
      approver_roles: [sre, ops]
```
Jordan: Nice. Also emit structured log event to the audit stream: `{event: "soft_lift", key: "partner-123", granted_by: "Alex", reason: "etl backfill"}` so SIEM parses it.
Nina: Compliance: require an attestation field for any lift > 12h or > 50k tokens. Also a step-up MFA for approver (Okta push).
Maria: How will billing show this? Need cost estimate in modal and a flag on usage exports so finance can attribute extra spend to partner soft lifts.
Alex: We'll add `billing_tag: soft_lift` on tokens consumed during lift window. Downstream billing pipeline will pick it up.
Jordan: Telemetry hooks: want an aggregated dashboard: per-key soft lift count, tokens consumed, avg latency during lift, top callers. Can add to Console -> Key metrics.
Sam: Edge cases: 1) if infra saturates, soft-lift should auto-failover to lower-cost model or fall back to hard cap. 2) if multiple concurrent lifts across many keys we need a global soft-lift budget to protect cluster.
Alex: Good point. Propose a global soft-burst pool with admin cap and alerts. If global pool exhausted, deny new soft lifts and mark existing ones as throttled (emit `soft_lift.throttled`).
Maria: What about programmatic API to request lifts? We'll need endpoints + checks. We should rate-limit lift requests to avoid spam.
Sam: API endpoints: POST `/keys/{id}/soft_lifts` (body: reason, ttl, approver). Response = 202 + lift id if pending, 200 if auto-approved.
Nina: Ensure the API requires caller identity and is logged. Approver flows must be auditable.
Alex: I'll draft a design doc with the flows: console, API, enforcement, metrics, billing, security checklist. Next actions: Sam to sketch runtime changes, Jordan to mock telemetry panels, Nina to list compliance constraints, Maria to mock modal.
Sam: I'll put a prototype of the token-bucket + soft-burst in a branch and link PR.
Jordan: I'll add dashboard wireframes and alert rules to the metrics board.
Nina: I'll list required audit fields + retention and MFA trigger conditions.
Maria: I'll mock the modal in Figma and attach copy.
Alex: Thanks all. If anyone has concerns about auto-approve rules or global pool numbers, drop them here before EOW. :thumbsup:
audit-bot: [audit-log] soft_lift.request created by Alex for key partner-123 (ttl=3600s, reason="etl backfill").
